performance_metrics.expected_latency: sub-second to low-single-digit seconds depending on pytest runtime
performance_metrics.memory_usage_pattern: bounded by in-memory JSON payloads and pytest summary capture

notes: Generates a structured system status snapshot and derives `SYSTEM_STATUS.md` from that JSON-first source.

Collects component health, test summary, runtime-backed coverage inventory from the canonical coverage snapshot, knowledge-base metrics, integrity signals, runtime-backed resolver capabilities with explicit and inferred route examples, operator shortcuts with matching VS Code task labels, a data-driven system summary footer, and threshold-aware recommended actions from current workspace state.
Keeps the human-readable status artifact reproducible through a dedicated CLI entry point and derives `SYSTEM_SUMMARY.md` from the same governed status and shortcut model.

Validates the canonical snapshot and derived markdown through registered status-domain rules, including runtime-integrity checks for the explicit and inferred resolver example routes, so the governance report can govern itself.
Supports both targeted remediation with `status-check --fix` and aggregate remediation with `all --fix-status` while keeping workspace and knowledge-base validation read-only.
Also exposes `coverage-snapshot` so coverage percentages can be refreshed from a real `pytest-cov` run without forcing the aggregate governance report to execute that expensive step on every pass.
Below-threshold component coverage now surfaces as a first-class recommended action in the canonical status snapshot instead of only appearing in component-health flags.
The canonical snapshot `generated_at` field is derived deterministically from the freshest governed inputs instead of preserving a static legacy timestamp.
